data.intent: Unit tests: Day-Off Index window settings, partial weeks, average and breakdown

decisions.chosen: plain average of the per-phrase percent changes
decisions.detail: user: the index is the average of these 3 searches; each phrase is on its own 0-100 scale, so changes are averaged, not interest values
an average over fewer phrases would be a different index

decisions.decision: Old index columns (study_year, release_day, per-source lifts, source counts)
decisions.chosen: removed; the index is one row per window, no longer per study year
decisions.detail: user: scratch everything of the old Day-Off Index and redefine it

decisions.chosen: one row per window (index_window), was per study year
decisions.detail: user: one YoY comparison over a configurable window

decisions.chosen: breakdown column on the index row
decisions.detail: user: the index is always accompanied by its breakdown, never left to be discovered

decisions.chosen: average weekly interest over the current window vs the same weeks 52 weeks earlier, per phrase
decisions.detail: user: average daily search interest 1-15 Nov 2026 vs 1-15 Nov 2025, weekly is fine over the 2-week window; configurable start, end and number of weeks

decisions.chosen: excluded from the averages; the change is NULL unless both windows are complete
decisions.detail: a week still filling in would understate its average

decisions.chosen: 52 weeks back (364 days), so both windows start on a Sunday like Google's weeks

fct_day_off_index.reason: the declaration names no dimension, time or measure column, so there is nothing for a semantic model to carry
notes: key column descriptions are not carried onto entities: MetricFlow's schema has no description field for an entity

not derived (role key or attribute, which a semantic model has no element for): current_start_week, current_end_week, prior_start_week, prior_end_week, weeks, batch_id, phrase_count, phrases_available, breakdown
limitations: day_off_index: MetricFlow aggregates a measure over a time dimension, and the declaration names no time column, so it is not derived

fct_day_off_index_terms.content:
name: fct_day_off_index_terms
description: 'The Day-Off Index breakdown: one row per search phrase, with its average weekly US search interest over the current window, over the same weeks a year earlier, and the percent change. Population: Every phrase in the Trends snapshot the index reads (stg_trends__weekly).'
model: ref('fct_day_off_index_terms')
entities:
  - name: term
    type: primary
    expr: term
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          null_rule: never
dimensions:
  - name: geo
    type: categorical
    description: US.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          null_rule: never
config:
  meta:
    dex:
      population:
        rule: Every phrase in the Trends snapshot the index reads (stg_trends__weekly).
        parent:
          model: stg_trends__weekly
          key:
            term: term
      assumptions:
        - decision: What the index compares
          chosen: average weekly interest over the current window vs the same weeks 52 weeks earlier, per phrase
          evidence: request
          detail: 'user: average daily search interest 1-15 Nov 2026 vs 1-15 Nov 2025, weekly is fine over the 2-week window; configurable start, end and number of weeks'
          column: pct_change
        - decision: Partial or missing weeks
          chosen: excluded from the averages; the change is NULL unless both windows are complete
          evidence: default
          detail: a week still filling in would understate its average
          column: pct_change
        - decision: Week alignment
          chosen: 52 weeks back (364 days), so both windows start on a Sunday like Google's weeks
          evidence: default
          detail: 'canonical: 1-14 Nov 2026 vs 2-15 Nov 2025'
          column: prior_start_week
fct_day_off_index_terms.reason: fct_day_off_index_terms already has a semantic model ('fct_day_off_index_terms' in models/marts/semantic/day_off_index.yml); an authored definition is not overwritten or duplicated
notes: key column descriptions are not carried onto entities: MetricFlow's schema has no description field for an entity

not derived (role key or attribute, which a semantic model has no element for): batch_id, span_start, span_end, current_start_week, current_end_week, prior_start_week, prior_end_week, weeks, current_weeks_found, prior_weeks_found
metrics are not derived: a measure is what a column holds, a metric is a business definition, and that stays the author's
limitations: current_avg_interest: MetricFlow aggregates a measure over a time dimension, and the declaration names no time column, so it is not derived
prior_avg_interest: MetricFlow aggregates a measure over a time dimension, and the declaration names no time column, so it is not derived
pct_change: MetricFlow aggregates a measure over a time dimension, and the declaration names no time column, so it is not derived
